extracted.intended_audience: journalists, press officers, and public information officers covering AACR meetings and AACR-related research
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of AACR Newsroom requirements and resources for press coverage of AACR meetings and organizational initiatives, including embargoed-material access, media/press registration, and media resource policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for embargoed materials / Apply for Embargoed Access
rubrics_metrics.description: The AACR provides embargoed materials related to the AACR’s journals and organizational initiatives to credentialed news media to facilitate accurate and comprehensive reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credentialed news media must apply for embargoed access (see 'Apply for Embargoed Access'). Embargoed materials are intended to facilitate accurate, comprehensive reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalist registration requirement for meeting coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists planning to cover AACR meetings, including the AACR Annual Meeting, must register to receive embargoed press programs and other important communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should use the 'Request Media Registration' or 'Press and PIO Registration' processes to register; registration is required to receive press programs and key communications about meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo policy (and management of exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: AACR maintains an Embargo Policy that governs distribution and handling of embargoed materials, and there is a process for Embargo Policy Exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the official Embargo Policy and, if needed, consult the Embargo Policy Exceptions page for how exceptions are handled. Specific rules and timelines are provided on those linked policy pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official press programs for AACR scientific meetings and conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: AACR provides Official Press Programs from AACR scientific meetings and conferences to credentialed/registered press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access to official press programs typically requires media registration and/or embargoed access; these programs are the source for session recaps and other official meeting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photo, video, and audio recording policy for AACR events
rubrics_metrics.description: AACR has a 'Photo, Video, and Audio Recording Policy' that governs recording at meetings and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Media Resources (Photo, Video, and Audio Recording Policy) page for permitted recording practices, restrictions, and any required permissions when covering AACR events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media contacts and newsroom resources availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Newsroom provides media contacts, media resources (News Releases, Media Advisories, AACR Fast Facts, etc.), and an overview of available newsroom materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the listed media contacts (address, telephone, email) for press inquiries and to request materials; consult Media Resources for fact sheets, press release archives, and other assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press and PIO registration pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a dedicated 'Press and PIO Registration' resource for press and public information officers related to AACR meetings and communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press offices and PIOs should follow the Press and PIO Registration process to ensure access to press programs, embargoed materials, and other communications for institutional coverage.
